subject: Orchid AI renewal + capacity uplift — benchmarking and save plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@orchid.ai>; Mike Harper <mike.harper@orchid.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid AI renewal + capacity uplift — benchmarking and save plan

Hi Sara / Mike —

Thanks again for the time last week. I wanted to follow up with a lightweight plan to keep Orchid on our platform ahead of renewal and to address the performance questions your engineering team raised during the bakeoff. High level: we can offer a targeted capacity uplift (30% additional reserved qps for the first 3 months) plus a short-term term-adjusted credit to close pricing gaps while we demonstrate parity on throughput and tail latency.

Proposed immediate steps:
- You share the benchmark logs you ran (sample CSV or perf traces) — we can use those to reproduce on our harness. (If you prefer, upload to the S3 link I shared previously.)
- Karthik will run a confinement run against the exact request/seq distributions your logs show and deliver a one-page readout with expected token cost delta and latency percentiles.
- If we validate parity at P95/P99 we’ll lock the uplift and the term credit into a short addendum (3 months).

Draft economics: 10% term credit applied over first invoice period + 30% reserved capacity boost for 90 days. If adoption/traffic crosses the uplift window we’ll roll the uplift into the next renewal at a mutually agreed rate.

I’ve looped in Lauren and Marissa for commercial/contract work and Karthik for the technical reproducibility. Targeting a tidy outcome: engineering validation by next Tuesday (16th) and contractual addendum by the 19th so procurement has time.

Thanks — let me know if that sequence looks sensible and share the benchmark CSV when you have a minute.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachment: redwood-save-plan-v2.pdf (proposal stub)

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@orchid.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Harper <mike.harper@orchid.ai>; engineering@orchid.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid AI renewal + capacity uplift — benchmarking and save plan

Vivek —

Appreciate the quick follow up. We ran two shortened bakeoffs last week: one against Redwood (your hosted baseline) and one against CompetitorX. The high level from our infra team: CompetitorX shows ~18% lower cost per token on our workload and slightly better P99 for long-sequence chat.

I’ve attached the raw CSV from the smoke run; engineering will also drop the request traces into the shared bucket by EOD. Two asks from our side before we can sign to any addendum:
1) A reproducible run from you that shows comparable P95 and P99 on the same traces.
2) A procurement-friendly term sheet with explicit caps and rollback language — we can’t lock a 12-month renewal without a short escape if the production delta persists.

If you can get the reproducible readout and a short legal-friendly addendum draft to us by the 17th, procurement can commit to a fast signature cycle. Otherwise we may need to run a longer trial.

Thanks,
Sara
Head of Platform
Orchid AI

Attachment: orchid-benchmark-results.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@orchid.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid AI renewal + capacity uplift — benchmarking and save plan

Sara —

Thanks for the CSV. I pulled the sample traces and ran a targeted harness run against the same request/sequence distribution you provided. Summary of what I ran is attached (benchmark-harness-config.json) — key points below:
- Recreated request mix (60% short-chat, 30% multi-turn, 10% long-form generation)
- Used the same model variant you used in the CompetitorX run (we matched their quantization profile where possible)
- Warm KV cache for the long sequences to match your experiment setup

Preliminary results (short summary):
- Average token cost delta: Redwood ~ +6% vs CompetitorX on this workload (we see that gap shrink with the uplifted reserved capacity profile).
- P95 latency: within 3–5% on all buckets.
- P99 latency: Redwood trails by ~12% on the exact long-sequence tail in the smoke run; however when we applied a 30% reserved capacity uplift (the configuration Vivek proposed) the P99 gap dropped to ~4% and average unit cost delta to ~+1%.

Recommendations:
1) Run the uplifted capacity smoke in your staging for 72 hours (we can provision the uplift with a single click).
2) If the staging run produces similar tail behavior you can accept the 3-month term credit + uplift and we’ll roll to long-term terms at renewal.

I’ve attached the harness config and the raw run logs. Happy to run a mirrored CompetitorX repro if you can share their exact model/quantization flags — otherwise the uplift test is the fastest path.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: benchmark-harness-config.json, run-20250915-log.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@orchid.ai>, Mike Harper <mike.harper@orchid.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid AI renewal + capacity uplift — benchmarking and save plan

Sara / Mike —

Great to see the uplift test is the path forward. Based on Karthik’s run we’re locking the proposed commercial terms into a short addendum (attached PDF). Key commercial bullets inside the addendum:
- 90-day reserved capacity uplift: +30% reserved qps starting on activation date.
- One-time term credit: 10% applied to first post-activation invoice.
- Early rollback clause: if P99 tail remains >10% worse than CompetitorX for two consecutive 24h windows during the uplift window, Orchid may opt to terminate the uplift and revert to baseline; in that case pricing reverts and we’ll pro-rate credits.
- Signature: single DocuSign form for both parties (link below).

Next steps to close this week:
1) Sara — confirm you want us to activate the 90-day uplift in your staging environment (we’ll need an OK from engineering to mirror traffic).
2) Mike — once staging is green, I’ll send the DocuSign link to procurement and your countersign path.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/0000000/deal/000000000

If you confirm staging activation by EOD Friday (19th) we’ll target procurement signature and production activation the following Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-save-plan-v2.pdf
